summary: An excerpt from a fiction novel, Book 14 part 104, narrated by a nineteen-year-old Black student who is stopped by two police officers while biking home after a curfew deadline. The narrator explains the danger of being stopped, the "Talk" given by Monica, and the fear of being checked against family history. The stop ends with a five-minute warning, and the narrator reaches home shaken but relieved, still thinking about the earlier arrest of a brother.
one_line: A nineteen-year-old narrator is stopped by police near curfew, recalling the racial dangers and family stakes behind the encounter.
key_facts: The narrator tells the officer they attend Horizons Technical Academy and that they are nineteen years old.
The narrator carries a state photo ID tucked in the back of their phone case.
The narrator obtained the state photo ID as soon as they turned nineteen.
The curfew for fourteen-year-olds is an hour earlier than the curfew for those who are older, which is why the narrator wanted proof of age.
The narrator fears the officer might run their name and find a relation to an alleged terrorist, though the narrator has no record.
Monica gave the narrator the Talk soon after the narrator went to live with her.
The narrator says the Talk for a Black person means being told to act respectful and submissive because police are allowed to kill those who do not.
The officer tells the narrator they have five minutes to get home or they will be taken to juvenile supervision.
The officer warns that the narrator's aunt would face a serious fine if the narrator is seen on the street one minute later.
This stop was the first time the narrator had been stopped by police since the narrator's brother was arrested.
After the brother's arrest, the narrator began harnessing the skills of the Group and friends to rescue him.
By the time the narrator reached the top of the steps, the adrenaline rush had turned into a giddy sense of relief.
